source.quote: Let $\epsilon \in [0,1)$. For any $i \in \{1,\hdots, K\}$ let $\E_i$ be the expectation against the joint distribution of rewards where all arms are i.i.d. Bernoulli of parameter $\frac{1-\epsilon}{2}$ but arm $i$, which is i.i.d. Bernoulli of parameter $\frac{1+\epsilon}{2}$. Then, for any forecaster, $$\max_{i}  \E_i \sum_{t=1}^n (Y_{i,t} - Y_{I_t,t}) \geq n \epsilon \left(1 - \frac{1}{K} - \sqrt{\epsilon \ln\frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}}  \sqrt{\frac{n}{2 K}}\right)$$

source.label: thm:mle_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1/8)$. Fix $\X, \Z \subset \R^d$ and $\Theta = \R^d$. Fix a problem $\theta \in \Theta$. Then, if the non-interactive MLE is $\delta$-PAC wrt $(\X, \Z, \Theta)$ where a different allocation can be used for each $\theta \in \Theta$, then it uses at least $c( \gamma^*+\rho^{\ast}\log(1/\delta))$ samples for the instance $(\X, \Z, \theta)$ where $c > 0$ is a universal constant.

notes: Delta_min is the smallest gap among items in Z. Algorithm is computationally inefficient for exponentially large Z.

If $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all policies $\psi$ and every $T \geq r^2$, ${\rm Risk} \left( T, \psi \right) \geq 0.006 \,r\, \sqrt{T}$.

notes: Regret is defined conditionally on Z=z through means: pseudo-regret. Worst case over z (z unbounded norm).

notes: Corollary 3.3 specializes to the unit sphere with standard normal noise with an absolute constant a_3 (same form, not recorded separately). Computation of greedy argmax not discussed.

notes: Algorithm assumed to be MLSE (corollary follows Theorem 1).

source.label: thm:linear_bandit_info_gain
source.quote: Consider a $d$-dimensional linear bandit with Gaussian noise. Let the action set $\actions \subseteq \{a \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|a\|_2 \le 1\}$. Let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a random vector with covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Then, for all $T \ge 1$ and all agents $\pi$, \infoGain{T}{\pi} \le \frac{1}{2} \log \det(I_d + \frac{T}{\sigma^2}\Sigma) + \frac{1}{2} = O(d \log T) = o(T).

notes: Information gain bound for any agent.

source.label: thm:mab_info_gain
source.quote: Consider a finite-armed bandit with Gaussian noise $W_{t+1} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$ and let $\theta \in \R^{|\actions|}$ be a random vector with finite covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Then for all $T\ge 1$ and all agents $\pi$, \infoGain{T}{\pi} \le \frac{1}{2} \log \det ( I_{|\actions|} + \frac{T }{\sigma^2}\Sigma ) + \frac{1}{2} = O(|\actions|\log T)=o(T).

notes: Information gain bound; adapted from Vakili et al. Theorem 3.

Consequently, if $\delta_D \to 0$ ... \sup_{\pi}\infoGain{T}{\pi} = o(T).
